subject: Where do warning messages come from in the object structure

messages.author: 5300e1c43e666524
messages.subject: Where do warning messages come from in the object structure
parts:
I am trying to build a loop that removes all models that did not converge or are suspect, and then use my new model list in AICcModAvg. I have figured out how to do it for convergences using the convergence slot in the object structure (shared code below, sorry if its sloppy), but I am having trouble finding out where the warning messages comes from. Is there a slot in the object structure that indicates a warning message has been thrown? I see a slot for "message", but this doesn't seem to be what I am looking for. Thanks for the help.

#convergence
#check convergence
model.list=list(list out models here)

#looping to pull out models that do not converge
conv=NULL
for (i in 1:n){
  conv[i]=model.list[[i]]@opt$convergence==0
}

#New model list
model.list.2=model.list[conv]


#New model names with only those that converge
Modnames <-c(list of model names)

Modnames.2=Modnames[conv]

#Model Selection for p structure
Cand.mods <- append(m0,model.list.2)
Modnames <-Modnames.2

aicctab <- aictab(cand.set=Cand.mods.p, modnames=Modnames.p, second.ord=TRUE, nobs=NULL, sort=TRUE, c.hat=1)

parts:
Thanks, Richard for your response. 

What I am trying to do is figure if my SE's for psi, col, and ext contain NaN (with code and not by scrolling through all the model summaries). I was hoping there would be a way to capture the warning within the object structure for each model, but that doesn't seem possible. Then I went to the source code and tried figuring out where the SE, Z and p estimates are stored in the structure so I could maybe capture those values and look for NaN's. Working with S4 classes is a bit beyond my R ability, so its been a struggle. I think what I am trying to do seems easier than it actually is.

What I am essentially trying to do is figure out which models, from a list of models, are not converging or have inestimable SE's. I have figured out how to do this with convergence within the object structure, but am having trouble with the SE's. Below is obviously wrong, but I am trying to figure out how to extract the SE column from this part of the model. My basic understanding of extracting columns and rows doesn't work for S4 objects (e.g., m15[,3]) and so I am at a bit of a loss.

> m15[1]
Initial:
                Estimate  SE   z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)        7.511 NaN NaN     NaN
as.factor(trt)2    0.082 NaN NaN     NaN
as.factor(trt)3   -5.099 NaN NaN     NaN
as.factor(trt)4   -4.799 NaN NaN     NaN

I've tried the following, I know its wrong; however its essentially what I am trying to do.

m15.psi=m15[1]
m15.psi[,3]==NaN

This way I can run a loop through all of my models and eliminate the ones that did not converge.

Cheers.

Travis

Thank you Nicholas and Richard!!!! Figuring out this little trick has saved me a week (or more) of work. I have copied some sample code below for anyone that may find it useful. Its probably pretty sloppy for those more privy to coding, but I gave it my best shot. Thanks again!

#check convergence
model.list=list(fm1,fm2,fm2,...so on)

#looping to pull out models that do not converge or have SE's that are NaN
conv=NULL
se.nan=NULL
for (i in 1:length(model.list)){
conv[i]=model.list[[i]]@opt$convergence==0
se.nan[i]=any(is.nan(SE(model.list[[i]])))

}

#New model list
model.list.2=model.list[conv]
Cand.mods=model.list.2[se.nan != "TRUE"]
#New model names with only those that converge

Modnames <-c("fm1",
               "fm2",
               "fm3",..so on
              )

Modnames.2=Modnames[conv] 
Modnames=Modnames.2[se.nan !="TRUE"]

aicctab <- aictab(cand.set=Cand.mods, modnames=Modnames, second.ord=TRUE, nobs=NULL, sort=TRUE, c.hat=1)
aicctab

parts:
Hi Travis et al,

I thought I share some code as well here as it seems fitting. The attached file includes a function that fits model combinations, but other than dredge it does not fit all possible combinations but rather searches the model space using AIC values. For each iteration of the outer loop it tries to fit a model adding (in this case) site specific covariates on the psi side, lists them, compares AIC values and retains the models within AICcut from the top model for the next iteration. It also tests for model convergence and NAN's. Its a work in progress but I have used and worked on this sporadically over the last couple years, so hopefully its somewhat tested. It would be great if others that find this useful could give it a try and let me know what they think or if there are any bugs apparent.

Below example code of how to use the function.

Cheers,
Richard

source("f.AIC_cut.occu.sig.used.15.08.11.r")

covar <- read.csv("site_covars.csv")
obs.covar <- read.csv("obs_covars.csv")
SiteCovarSet<-as.vector(c("SC1","SC2","SC3","SC4","SC5"))

MyOccuData<- unmarkedFrameOccu(y,siteCovs=covar, obsCov=obs.covar)

um.frame <- MyOccuData
fm.p <- occu(~OC1+OC2+OC3 ~1, data=um.frame)

#use function from sourced file above
f.occ <- f.AICc.occu.sig(fm.p, SiteCovarSet, max.iter=20, AICcut=2, ,um.frame=MyOccuData)

#optional: remove models where p-values for estimates are higher than p.crit
f.occ.sig <- occu.rem.non.sig(f.occ,p.crit=0.15)
f.occ.sig.sub <- occu.subset(f.occ.sig,cutoff=7)

#model averaging: the else part is only needed if f.AICc.occu.sig returned only one model
if (length(f.occ.sig.sub)>1){
  f.occ.avg <- model.avg(f.occ.sig.sub)
  f.occ.avg <- add.coefmat(f.occ.avg)
} else {
  f.occ.avg <- f.occ.sig.sub

}
